blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Video generation and feed-forward 3D reconstruction typically use separate representations, requiring RGB decoding and visual re-encoding to recover geometry from generated latents. We propose Latent Bridge, which connects video generative latent spaces with geometric feature spaces to directly predict 3D geometry from video latents. We develop representation-specific bridges for Wan2.1 and V-RAE, enabling feed-forward prediction of cameras, depth, and 3D point clouds without the intermediate RGB pathway. Each bridge is trained on RGB videos through feature distillation, while the video encoder and geometry model remain frozen. Training requires neither ground-truth geometry nor execution of the downstream geometric aggregator or prediction heads. At inference, the same video latents support both RGB decoding and geometry prediction. The same trained bridge can be reused for image-to-video and text-to-video generation within the same video latent space, without bridge retraining. Experiments on Co3Dv2 and WildRGB-D demonstrate competitive geometric reconstruction quality, efficient end-to-end generation and reconstruction, and faster latent-to-geometry decoding, highlighting latent alignment as a practical and reusable interface between video generation and 3D reconstruction. Our code is available at: https://github.com/hustvl/Latent-Bridge.
blocks.zh: 视频生成和feed-forward 3D重建通常使用单独的表达方式,要求RGB解码和视觉重编码从产生的潜伏物中恢复几何. 我们提出Latent Bridge,将视频基因潜伏空间与几何特征空间连接起来,从视频潜伏中直接预测3D几何. 我们为Wan2.1和V-RAE开发具有代表性的桥梁,从而能够对摄像机、深度和没有中间RGB路径的3D点云进行向导预测。 每座桥通过特征蒸馏对RGB视频进行培训,而视频编码器和几何模型仍然冷冻. 培训既不需要地面真实几何,也不需要执行下游几何聚合器或预测头。 推论,同样的视频潜伏支持RGB解码和几何预测. 同样的训练有素的桥可以在同一个视频潜在空间内用于图像到视频和文本到视频生成,而无需桥面再培训. Co3Dv2和WildRGB-D的实验展示了具有竞争力的几何重建质量,高效的端对端生成与重建,以及更快的潜伏到几何解码,强调潜在对接是视频生成与3D重建之间的实用和可重复使用的界面. 我们的代码见:https://github.com/hustvl/Latent-Bridge。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Recent advances in video generation and feed-forward 3D reconstruction
have enabled compelling visual synthesis and efficient geometric inference.
Video generation models, such as CogVideoX ( Yang et al., 2025 ) and Wan2.1 ( Wan et al., 2025 ) , combine spatiotemporally compressed
latent representations with diffusion transformers to synthesize
high-quality, temporally coherent videos.
Meanwhile, feed-forward reconstruction models, such as
VGGT ( Wang et al., 2025 ) , jointly predict camera parameters,
depth maps, and 3D point maps from multi-view images in a single forward pass.
Recent work has begun to explore the joint execution of these two tasks: generating videos while simultaneously reconstructing the generated content.

blocks.en:
Despite their complementary goals, video generation and feed-forward
3D reconstruction typically rely on different representations.
Video generators synthesize content in spatiotemporally compressed
latent spaces, whereas reconstruction models often aggregate
features from visual foundation models such as
DINOv2 ( Oquab et al., 2024 ) to infer scene geometry.
This representational gap means that combining the two models
typically involves decoding generated latents into RGB frames
and re-encoding them into geometric features, introducing
additional computation. This raises the question: Can scene geometry be generated directly without RGB decoding?

blocks.en:
Recent work has begun to integrate video generation with explicit geometry prediction. Gen3R ( Huang et al., 2026 ) compresses intermediate VGGT features into geometric latents, aligns their distribution with video appearance latents, and fine-tunes a video diffusion model to jointly generate both. As shown in Fig. 1 (a), joint generation in a shared latent space requires additional training and can reduce efficiency due to the increased number of tokens.
FantasyWorld ( Dai et al., 2026 ) introduces a geometric branch into video generation. VGGRPO ( An et al., 2026 ) uses latent-space geometry predictions to construct rewards for video model post-training, while Beyond Pixels ( Liu et al., 2026 ) combines latent alignment, LoRA adaptation, and geometry-supervised fine-tuning of prediction heads for direct latent-to-4D prediction. As shown in Fig. 1 (b), these methods all aim to train a 3D/4D decoder module, requiring substantial data and retraining of the decoder, while also raising concerns about generalization.

FantasyWorld (Dai et al., 2026)将几何分支引入视频生成. VGGRPO(An等人,2026年)使用潜在空间几何预测来构建视频模型后训练的奖励,而Beyond Pixels(Liu等人,2026年)结合了潜在对齐,LORA适应,以及几何监督的预测头的微调,用于直接潜到4D的预测. 如图1(b)所示,这些方法都旨在培训一个3D/4D解码器模块,需要大量数据和对解码器进行再培训,同时引起对通用性的关注.

blocks.en: Unlike the aforementioned methods, we argue that the key lies in aligning the generative and reconstruction latent spaces. We propose Latent Bridge, which directly maps video latents into the representation space of a frozen feed-forward geometry model (Fig. 1 (c)). The frozen downstream VGGT aggregator and depth head can then be used to reconstruct the scene. This provides an elegant solution that eliminates the need for joint feature training or training downstream decoder heads. It also generalizes well, enabling the reuse of existing generative models and downstream tasks built on the same representation. Specifically, we adapt our framework to two representative video encoders, the Wan2.1 VAE and V-RAE ( Guo et al., 2026 ) , by designing a dedicated Bridge network for each. This enables models built upon either encoder to directly generate scene geometry.

blocks.en: Our contributions can be summarized as follows: • We propose Latent Bridge, which aligns the generative latent space with the representation space of a reconstruction model, enabling geometry to be recovered directly from generated latents. The Bridge module is trained through feature distillation and requires only video data for training. This substantially reduces the cost of recovering geometry from the latent spaces of generative models. • We adapt our framework to two video encoders, Wan2.1 and V-RAE, by designing a dedicated Latent Bridge network for each. Both variants achieve strong performance, demonstrating that the Latent Bridge framework can effectively accommodate different generative latent spaces. • Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed Latent Bridge enables high-quality and efficient reconstruction. It also exhibits strong generalization: within the same latent space, it can support generative models designed for different generation tasks, as well as other downstream tasks, without retraining.

blocks.en:
Modern video generation models commonly extend latent diffusion to the
spatiotemporal domain, where a video VAE compresses RGB frames into compact
latent representations and a diffusion transformer models their temporal
dynamics. Stable Video Diffusion ( Blattmann et al., 2023 ) establishes a
scalable latent video diffusion framework, while
HunyuanVideo ( Kong et al., 2024 ) demonstrates the effectiveness of
large diffusion transformers and progressive training for high-fidelity video
generation. Wan2.1 ( Wan et al., 2025 ) follows this paradigm and combines a
causal spatiotemporal VAE with a diffusion transformer to support both
text-to-video and image-to-video generation. REPA ( Yu et al., 2025 ) and VA-VAE ( Yao et al., 2025 ) align diffusion features and VAE latents, respectively, with pretrained
visual representations to improve generative modeling.
RAE ( Zheng et al., 2026 ) directly adopts frozen visual encoders,
while V-RAE ( Guo et al., 2026 ) extends this paradigm to video through
temporal pooling.

blocks.en: Recent work has explored video and 3D co-generation through complementary approaches. FantasyWorld ( Dai et al., 2026 ) couples video and geometry latents through a trainable geometry branch on a frozen Wan2.1 backbone, while LYRA ( Bahmani et al., 2026 ) introduces a self-distilled 3D Gaussian decoder. Gen3R ( Huang et al., 2026 ) jointly generates video and geometry in a unified latent space, whereas PixWorld ( Gao et al., 2026a ) operates in pixel space to avoid VAE-induced detail loss. VGGT-World ( Sun et al., 2026 ) instead forecasts geometry-centric VGGT tokens and decodes future geometry using frozen heads, without synthesizing RGB frames. VGGRPO ( An et al., 2026 ) uses latent-space geometry predictions to construct rewards for video DiT post-training, while Beyond Pixels ( Liu et al., 2026 ) directly decodes geometry from video latents. VIST3A ( Go et al., 2026 ) connects video latents to a selected intermediate reconstruction layer and jointly trains the stitching layer and downstream LoRA adapters using teacher-predicted geometry. Pano2World ( Li et al., 2026 ) aligns diffusion hidden features with a pretrained reconstruction model’s token space through feature distillation, followed by joint fine-tuning of the adapter and Gaussian decoder under rendering supervision. In contrast, we map video latents to a predefined geometric feature interface through feature alignment, keeping the downstream geometric aggregator and prediction heads entirely frozen.

blocks.en: 4 Method
blocks.zh: 4 方法

blocks.en: We propose an alignment framework between generative latents and the representations of a feed-forward geometry model, which we term the Latent Bridge . The key idea is to jointly support video generation and 3D reconstruction by aligning generative and reconstruction representations, without retraining the existing vision autoencoder, generative model, or 3D reconstruction heads. For the Wan2.1 VAE and V-RAE, we design distinct Latent Bridge networks and develop a corresponding training procedure, as illustrated in Fig. 2 . At inference, the bridge enables the frozen geometry model to predict 3D geometry directly from generated video latents.

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en: We presented Latent Bridge, a framework that connects video generation and feed-forward 3D reconstruction through latent-space feature alignment. By mapping Wan2.1 and V-RAE video representations to a predefined geometric feature interface, our method enables direct prediction of cameras, depth, and point clouds while keeping the downstream geometric model frozen. This design bypasses RGB decoding and visual re-encoding in the geometry branch, allowing a shared video latent representation to support both video synthesis and geometry prediction. Experiments on Co3Dv2 and WildRGB-D demonstrate competitive reconstruction quality with improved inference efficiency. More broadly, our results suggest that feature alignment offers a practical route to reusing pretrained geometric models with generative video representations.
blocks.zh: 我们提出了Latent Bridge,这个框架通过潜在空间特性对接,连接视频生成和向导的3D重建。 通过将Wan2.1和V-RAE的视频表示图映射到一个预先定义的几何特征界面,我们的方法可以直接预测相机、深度和点云,同时将下游几何模型冻结。 这种设计绕过RGB在几何分支中的解码和视觉重编码,允许共享视频潜伏的表示支持视频合成和几何预测. Co3Dv2和WildRGB-D的实验显示,具有竞争力的重建质量提高了推论效率. 更广义地说,我们的结果表明,特征调整为重新使用预先训练过的几何模型提供了一条实用的路线,并带有基因图象。

blocks.en: A.1 Comparison with Existing Methods
blocks.zh: A.1 与现有方法的比较

blocks.en: As shown in Tab. 5 , we compare our method with existing approaches from two perspectives: compatibility with existing models and training overhead. Cross-DiT checkpoint reuse refers to whether the method can produce 3D outputs using different generative DiT checkpoints without retraining. FantasyWorld trains a geometry branch and cross-branch adapters while keeping the video backbone frozen, whereas Gen3R fine-tunes the video DiT to jointly generate appearance and geometry latents. Beyond Pixels and our method instead learn geometry pathways from video latents without updating the DiT, enabling reuse across compatible generators that share the same VAE checkpoint and latent conventions. We demonstrate this reuse by applying the same Wan Bridge checkpoint to camera-conditioned generation and the official Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B model without additional Bridge training. Pretrained task-head reuse refers to the ability to reuse existing downstream heads because our method outputs features in VGGT’s DINO feature space. Consequently, the resulting features can be used not only for reconstruction with VGGT but also for cross-view segmentation with VGGT-S, as shown in Section A.2 . Gen3R reconstructs intermediate VGGT geometry tokens, which are decoded by pretrained geometry heads. In contrast, FantasyWorld and Beyond Pixels incorporate their decoder heads into training and therefore do not offer this advantage. Therefore, our method offers substantially greater versatility than existing approaches.

FantasyWorld在保持视频骨干冷冻的同时,会训练一个几何分支和跨分支适配器,而Gen3R则微调视频DiT,共同生成外观和几何潜质. 除了像素和我们的方法之外,我们还可以在不更新DiT的情况下从视频潜伏处学习几何路径,从而能够重复使用具有相同VAE检查站和潜伏常规的兼容发电机。 我们通过将同一个Wan桥检查站用于照相机的生成和没有额外桥面训练的官方Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B模型来证明这种再利用。 预先训练的任务头再利用是指重新使用现有下游头的能力,因为我们的方法输出在VGGT的DINO特征空间中具有特征. 因此,如A.2节所示,由此产生的特征不仅可用于VGGT的重建,而且可用于VGGT-S的交叉视图分割。 Gen3R重建中间的VGGT几何符号,它们由预先训练的几何头解码. 相比之下,"最终幻想世界"(Fantasy World)和"超越像素"(Beyond Pixels)将它们的解码头纳入训练,因此没有提供这种优势. 因此,我们的方法比现有方法多得多。

blocks.en: In addition, we compare the additional training costs required to support both generation and reconstruction. FantasyWorld trains a geometry branch and cross-branch adapters, while Gen3R fine-tunes the video DiT for joint video and geometry generation. Beyond Pixels trains an alignment module, LoRA adapters, and geometry prediction heads. In contrast, we train only the Bridge through feature alignment, keeping the video encoder, geometric aggregator, and prediction heads frozen. Keeping the decoder heads frozen further reduces the training cost. Furthermore, FantasyWorld and Gen3R introduce additional geometry tokens. Our bridge is trained using feature supervision alone, without executing the downstream geometric aggregator or prediction heads during optimization.

To compare the alignment efficiency of feature supervision with that of geometry supervision provided through the frozen decoder heads, we conduct an experiment, as shown in Table 6 .
Our feature-supervised bridge requires only 0.166 s and 3.17 GiB per forward–loss–backward pass, compared with 5.896 s and 31.27 GiB for geometry supervision with frozen VGGT- Ω \Omega . blocks.en: Beyond geometry reconstruction, we extend our framework to the standard VGGT feature space and examine downstream reuse. This experiment uses a separately trained VGGT-aligned Bridge, rather than the VGGT- Ω \Omega Bridge evaluated above. Within the VGGT-aligned branch, the Bridge checkpoint used for geometry reconstruction also supports cross-view segmentation through a frozen pretrained VGGT-S ( Gao et al., 2026b ) module. This reuse requires only resolution and feature-interface adjustments, without additional training or fine-tuning. As shown in Fig. 6 , given a first-frame object mask, the pipeline propagates masks across generated frames without decoding the generated video into RGB. We present additional results in Fig. 7 . Associating these masks with the predicted 3D coordinates further produces label-colored object point clouds. These results demonstrate task reuse within the VGGT-aligned branch, beyond its original geometry application.

blocks.en: A.4 Limitation.
blocks.zh: A.4 限制。

blocks.en:
Our Bridge network has the following limitations:
First, our model depends on a pretrained geometry model.
The bridge learns to match teacher features while keeping the downstream geometry model frozen, and therefore cannot be expected to correct the teacher’s geometric errors. Second, inconsistencies in generated videos are not automatically corrected. Our method extracts geometry from generated latents but does not explicitly constrain the video generation process. Therefore, if the generated content exhibits structural changes or object inconsistencies across frames, the Bridge cannot guarantee the reconstruction of a coherent 3D scene.
